open_questions: Whether Fresno's Ordinance 2025-40 (https://documents.fresno.gov/WebLink/DocView.aspx?id=21170101&dbid=0&repo=LF-Repository) adds local amendments to Section 11-104 (2025 California Electrical Code) or adopts it as-is could not be confirmed from the indexed snippet; opening the full Ordinance 2025-40 PDF would settle it.

Whether Fresno still enforces the 1991 homeowner written electrical examination requirement in Ordinance 1991-002 could not be confirmed; opening the Owner Builder Checklist PDF linked on https://www.fresno.gov/planning/building-and-safety/building-permit-center/ would settle it.

No City of Fresno residential electrical load calculation worksheet, EV charger load factor, or single-family standby generator plan-check threshold was found in indexed PDFs; opening the Electric Vehicle Charging Submittal Checklist and Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Handout on https://www.fresno.gov/planning/applications-forms-fees/ and Page 2 of https://www.fresno.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/New-Residential-Solar-Plan-Check-Submittal.pdf would settle EV and solar/storage load calculation requirements.

The agency name in the prompt ('Development and Resource Management Department') has been renamed on fresno.gov to 'Planning and Development Department, Building and Safety Services Division' (https://www.fresno.gov/planning/building-and-safety/), though some older contact emails still use DARM.building@fresno.gov.

The Owner Builder Checklist PDF linked on https://www.fresno.gov/planning/building-and-safety/building-permit-center/ could not be opened directly to verify whether Fresno still enforces the 1991 homeowner written electrical examination requirement from Ordinance 1991-002 (https://documents.fresno.gov/WebLink/edoc/4030353/Ordinance%20-%201991-002%20-%20181991.pdf?dbid=0&repo=LF-Repository).

The Electric Vehicle Charging Submittal Checklist and Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Handout PDFs linked on https://www.fresno.gov/planning/applications-forms-fees/ could not be opened directly to confirm whether they apply to single-family residential Level 2 chargers or only commercial/multifamily installations.

Page 2 of the New Residential Solar Plan Check Submittal Checklist (https://www.fresno.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/New-Residential-Solar-Plan-Check-Submittal.pdf) was not fully indexed to verify whether single-line diagram or battery storage (ESS) requirements are itemized on page 2.

No dedicated City of Fresno residential permit checklists were found for standalone standby/portable generators, subpanels, or 240 V appliance circuits (hot tubs, saunas, heat pumps), nor any city-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet or EV charger load factor.
